newsitem.title: USA: Access Health plunges on lower earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: Access Health plunges on lower earnings forecast.

text.p: Access Health Inc. lost more than a third of its market value Wednesday after it said it expected its fiscal 1997 earnings to fall as much as 17 percent below analysts' estimates.

Shares in Access Health, which is based in Rancho Cordova, Calif., plunged by $8, or 36 percent, to $14.625 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market, where it was one of the most actively traded issues.

The company, which provides membership-based personal health care management services, said after the stock market closed Tuesday that it believed its fiscal 1997 earnings will be between 15 cents and 17 cents below the consensus estimate of 99 cents a share.
For the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, Access reported net income of $8.13 million, or 61 cents a share.
It added that it expected its revenues for the fiscal year will be about 10 percent to 15 percent below analyst expectations.
The company said sales were hurt by slower membership enrollment growth and a decision by BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee to discontinue certain services to some of its Medicaid population.
Access also said sales were hurt by a competitive pricing environment for its core products.
